words.childMeaning: A long vehicle that travels on metal tracks.
practiceSentences: The train has many long carriages.
When does the train arrive?
Theo, I can see the train!
I wave at the passing train.
A train carries people to another town.

words.childMeaning: A snail is a small animal that carries a shell on its back.
practiceSentences: Nora found a snail on the wet garden path.
The snail moved slowly across the leaf.
A snail carries its shell wherever it goes.
Leo watched a snail climb the flower pot.
The snail hid inside its shell when it rained.

words.childMeaning: The part at the back of an animal's body that can move.
practiceSentences: The cat curled its tail around its paws.
Amal drew a long tail on her paper fish.
A monkey can hang from a branch by its tail.
The puppy wagged its tail when Leo came home.
That bird has bright feathers in its tail.

words.childMeaning: To sail means to travel on water in a boat.
practiceSentences: We will sail across the lake in a small boat.
The little boat can sail when the wind blows.
Amal watched the ships sail out to sea.
Grandpa taught Leo how to sail.
They sail to the island every summer.

words.childMeaning: To stay in one place until something happens.
practiceSentences: She could not wait for the next partner activity at school.
She could not wait for Saturday, when a brand new school week would begin.
"Wait," she said kindly.
Amal and her classmates could hardly wait.
She could not wait for morning, so she could watch them again.

words.childMeaning: The order word for number 2, straight after the first.
practiceSentences: Nora sat in the second row beside the window.
Which day is the second day of your school week?
“Take the second book on the shelf,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I finished second in the counting race.
The second of June is written as 2nd of June.

words.childMeaning: A minute is a short amount of time, sixty seconds long.
practiceSentences: It only took a minute to finish the puzzle.
Can you hold this for just a minute?
Adam ran around the garden in under a minute.
The kettle boiled in about a minute.
The clock ticks sixty times in one minute.

words.childMeaning: An hour is a unit of time made up of sixty minutes.
practiceSentences: Adam finished his homework in an hour.
How long is an hour?
Amal read her book for a whole hour.
The shadow moves a little every hour.
We waited an hour for the bus to come.

words.childMeaning: A group of seven days that follow one after another.
practiceSentences: Amal learned something new on every day of her first week.
How many days are there in one week?
“You had a wonderful first week,” said Amal's mother.
I visit my grandmother once a week.
A new week starts again after Friday.

words.childMeaning: One of the twelve parts of a year.
practiceSentences: February is the shortest month of the year.
In which month were you born?
“My birthday is in the month of June,” said Leo.
I count the days until my favourite month.
Each month has its own page on the calendar.

words.childMeaning: A year is twelve months, from January to December.
practiceSentences: There are twelve months in one year.
Leo grew taller this year.
We plant new seeds every year.
Last year Amal learned to ride a bike.
The new year starts in January.

words.childMeaning: Early means before the usual time, near the start.
practiceSentences: In a small town near the sea, Amal woke up early.
Leo came to school early to help Teacher Yasmin.
The birds sing early in the morning.
We left early so we would not be late.
Grandpa waters the garden early every day.

words.childMeaning: Soon means that something will happen after a short time.
practiceSentences: Soon the smoke was gone.
The rain will stop soon.
Amal will see her cousin soon.
Dinner will be ready soon.
Soon the little plant grew two green leaves.

words.childMeaning: Again means one more time, after doing it before.
practiceSentences: Birds began to visit again.
“Let me try again,” said Leo.
Amal read her old work again.
The sun was low again, and Amal's shadow grew long.
She shook the red rug outside so that it was clean again.

words.childMeaning: Next means the thing that comes right after this one.
practiceSentences: What happens next in the story?
Leo sat next to his best friend.
Nora, you go next!
The next page showed a picture of a lion.
Nora put up her hand next.

words.childMeaning: Then means next, or after that.
practiceSentences: Then came the surprise.
Then came two small leaves.
“Then we are a team,” she said.
Then Amal made her new booklet.
Then Leo passed the stick to Amal.

words.childMeaning: Past means going by something, or a time that has already gone.
practiceSentences: Amal ran past him.
“It is half past two,” said Amal to herself.
The bus went past our house.
Leo walked past the market on his way home.
In the past, people wrote letters by hand.

words.childMeaning: The time that has not happened yet, coming after today.
practiceSentences: Amal draws a picture of her future classroom.
Nobody knows the future, so we plan carefully.
What job would you like in the future?
Adam said, "In the future I will build ships."
I save my coins for the future.

words.childMeaning: An adult is a person who has grown up.
practiceSentences: An adult helps the children cross the road.
Ask an adult to read the story with you.
Every adult in the hall clapped for the class.
An adult must sign the letter from school.
Leo asked an adult for help with the heavy box.

words.childMeaning: An aunt is the sister of your mother or father, or your uncle's wife.
practiceSentences: My aunt gave me a new pencil.
Does your aunt live near the river?
Look, Nora's aunt is planting a tree!
Our aunt helps us pick up litter.
"I can see three small brown birds in that bush," whispers his aunt.

words.childMeaning: An uncle is the brother of your mum or dad.
practiceSentences: Does your uncle live near the beach, Amal?
My uncle helped dig the holes for the trees.
Look, Theo's uncle brought a new spade!
Adam's uncle taught him how to plant seeds.
In the garden, Sami's father is planting trees with his uncle.

words.childMeaning: The child of your aunt or uncle.
practiceSentences: My cousin came to stay for the holiday.
Amal has a cousin who lives in the city.
Leo plays football with his cousin every Saturday.
Her cousin is the same age as she is.
We visit my cousin and my aunt on Fridays.

words.childMeaning: A mother or a father who looks after you.
practiceSentences: Every parent came to watch our class play.
A parent helps children learn right from wrong.
Which parent walks you to school each day?
Theo said, "My parent packed fresh fruit in my lunch."
I hug each parent before I sleep at night.

words.childMeaning: A person who lives near you, on your street or in your building.
practiceSentences: Every morning our neighbour Theo waves to us from his gate.
Who is the new neighbour in the house on the corner?
“Come and meet our neighbour,” said Mum, opening the front door.
My neighbour lends us her ladder when we clean the windows.
A good neighbour helps you carry your shopping up the stairs.

words.childMeaning: People means more than one person.
practiceSentences: He kept the people safe.
Come and meet the people in my neighbourhood.
People were buying fish, fruit and bright cloth.
“People cut them down for wood,” she said softly.
Many people were waiting at the bus stop.

words.childMeaning: A person is one human being, like you or me.
practiceSentences: Every person in the class has a name card.
Amal is a kind person who helps her friends.
Only one person can sit on this chair.
The first person in the line opens the door.
A person needs food, water and sleep.

words.childMeaning: Feeling happy and pleased about something good that has happened.
practiceSentences: Amal was glad to see birds back in the branches.
Are you glad that the rain has come at last?
“I am glad you came to help,” said Nora.
I am glad that my little tree has a flower.
We felt glad when the path was clean and tidy.

words.childMeaning: Polite means kind and well-mannered towards other people.
practiceSentences: It is polite to say please and thank you.
Amal was polite to the new girl in class.
Leo gave a polite answer to Teacher Yasmin.
Being polite makes other people feel happy.
She waited her turn to be polite.

words.childMeaning: Always telling the truth, even when it is hard.
practiceSentences: An honest pupil handed the lost purse to the school office.
Is it always easy to be honest with your friends?
“An honest heart sleeps peacefully,” said Grandma Hana.
I was honest when I forgot to finish my homework.
Rami the police officer thanked the honest boy who returned the wallet.

words.childMeaning: A promise is when you say you will really do something.
practiceSentences: Amal made a promise to water the plants.
“Let's promise something,” says Sami's mother.
Leo kept his promise to help Nora.
A promise is something you must not break.
I promise to be back before dark.

words.childMeaning: To invite someone means to ask them to come.
practiceSentences: Amal will invite her cousin to the party.
Did you invite Leo to your house?
We invite our neighbours for tea on Fridays.
Nora made cards to invite the whole class.
It is kind to invite someone who is alone.

words.childMeaning: Feeling glad for something good and wanting to say thank you.
practiceSentences: Amal felt thankful for the shade of the old tree.
What are you thankful for in nature today?
“We are thankful for the rain,” said the villagers.
I am thankful for the soil that feeds our food.
Being thankful helps us look after what we have.

words.childMeaning: Being kind to people and listening when they speak.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin earns our respect by listening carefully.
We show respect by listening when others speak.
How do you show respect to your grandparents?
Maya said, "Respect means waiting quietly for your turn."
I show respect when I greet my teacher politely.

words.childMeaning: To believe that someone is honest and will do what they say.
practiceSentences: Leila said her team could trust each other every day.
Do you trust your best friend with a secret?
Amal, I trust you to hold the kitten gently!
The children learned to trust the firefighter's advice.
Trust grows when people keep their promises.

words.childMeaning: To forgive means to stop being cross with someone.
practiceSentences: Amal chose to forgive Leo for breaking her pencil.
It is kind to forgive a friend who says sorry.
“Please forgive me,” said Nora quietly.
Grandma said we should forgive and stay friends.
Leo asked his sister to forgive him.

words.childMeaning: About means on the subject of something, or roughly.
practiceSentences: What is this book about?
Leo told his friend about his word hunt.
Tell me about your favourite animal!
There are about ten children in the group.
Listen to this story about Maya and her new partner, Nora.

words.childMeaning: Around means on every side of something, or turning to look in every direction.
practiceSentences: Maya turned around to see who was calling her.
Can you look around and find your pencil?
Nora walked around the garden twice.
There were books scattered around the room.
Maya looked around the room.

words.childMeaning: Each means every one, taken one at a time.
practiceSentences: Each runner passes a stick to the next one.
She loved her street because everyone helped each other.
She liked how they helped each other, just like a big family.
Read the poem and do each action as you say it: Reach for the sky!
Amal gave each friend a paper star.

words.childMeaning: Every means each one, with none left out.
practiceSentences: Every child in the class had a partner.
Did you read every page of the book?
Every morning, Amal walks to school with Nora.
We say hello to every visitor.
And every time we read a word, we learn something new.

words.childMeaning: If tells you what happens when something else is true.
practiceSentences: If it rains, we will stay inside.
Ask Teacher Yasmin if you need help.
If you are kind, you will make friends.
Leo will come if his mum says yes.
We can go to the park if the sun shines.

words.childMeaning: One of the seven parts of a week.
practiceSentences: Every school day begins with the register.
Which day of the week do you like best?
“Today is a busy day,” said Amal's mother.
I read for ten minutes every day.
The day after Wednesday is Thursday.

words.childMeaning: To stay means to keep still, or to remain in one place.
practiceSentences: Stay calm and do not wave your arms.
Amal will stay at her grandma's house tonight.
Please stay behind the yellow line.
The puppy learned to sit and stay.
We stay inside when the rain is heavy.

words.childMeaning: A flat container used for carrying or holding things.
practiceSentences: Leo carried his lunch on a blue tray.
Put the wet paint pots on the tray.
Nora filled a tray with small seeds.
The tray was too heavy for one person.
Grandma brought the tea in on a tray.

words.childMeaning: A key is a small metal thing that opens a lock.
practiceSentences: Mum turned the key in the front door.
Leo lost the key to his bicycle lock.
The key hangs on a hook in the kitchen.
Amal found a tiny key under the mat.
You need a key to open this gate.

words.childMeaning: To need something means you must have it.
practiceSentences: I need to find the hospital.
Plants need water and light to grow.
You need a coat when it is cold.
We need three more chairs for the table.
Leo said he did not need any help.

words.childMeaning: A person who grows food and looks after farm animals.
practiceSentences: The farmer fills the water trough before the sun gets hot.
How early does the farmer wake up to milk the cows?
“Mind the wet path,” the farmer said as we walked into the field.
I helped a farmer pick beans at my uncle's farm last year.
Every market day the farmer brings fresh vegetables into town.

words.childMeaning: A person who helps people who are ill and makes them better.
practiceSentences: Doctor Sarah works at the clinic beside the post office.
When did the doctor last check your ears, Maya?
“Open wide and say ah,” said the doctor with a smile.
My little brother Idris was not afraid of the doctor at all.
The doctor wrote a note so that I could rest at home for two days.

words.childMeaning: A person who cares for people who are ill or hurt.
practiceSentences: The nurse weighed the baby and wrote the number in a small blue book.
How many hours does a nurse work in one long night?
“You were very brave today,” the nurse told Mina.
I want to thank the nurse who looked after my grandmother.
At the school clinic a nurse checks our eyes every year.

words.childMeaning: A person who drives a car, a bus or a lorry.
practiceSentences: The bus driver, Nadia, waved.
The driver stopped so the children could cross.
Every driver must watch the road carefully.
Amal thanked the driver as she got off.
The lorry driver brought boxes to the shop.

words.childMeaning: The police are people whose job is to keep everyone safe.
practiceSentences: A police officer named Rami arrived on his bicycle.
The police help people who are lost.
We called the police when the dog ran away.
A police car has a bright blue light.
The police station is next to the library.

words.childMeaning: A person who has an important job keeping people safe.
practiceSentences: The officer helped the lost child find her mother.
Have you ever spoken to a police officer, Theo?
Rami, thank you for being such a kind officer!
The officer stood at the corner, watching the busy road.
An officer in a blue uniform stood at the gate.

words.childMeaning: A person who puts out fires and rescues people from danger.
practiceSentences: Two firefighters ran towards the smoke while everybody else moved back.
How long does a firefighter train before the first day at work?
“Stand well back, please,” the firefighter said to the crowd.
My cousin Noah wants to be a firefighter when he grows up.
A firefighter visited our class and showed us the fire engine hose.

words.childMeaning: A person who owns or looks after a shop and sells things.
practiceSentences: The shopkeeper stacks the tins neatly on the shelf each evening.
Does the shopkeeper open the door before eight o'clock?
“That will be five coins, please,” said the shopkeeper.
I counted my money carefully and gave it to the shopkeeper.
When the rain started, the shopkeeper pulled a cover over the fruit.

words.childMeaning: A baker is a person who makes bread and cakes.
practiceSentences: The baker starts work before the sun comes up.
Our baker makes fresh bread every morning.
Amal watched the baker shape the dough.
The baker gave Leo a warm bun.
A baker needs flour, water and a hot oven.

words.childMeaning: A worker is a person who does a job.
practiceSentences: Every worker at the market wears an apron.
The worker fixed the broken gate.
Each worker helps to keep our street clean.
A worker came to mend the school roof.
The workers stopped for lunch at noon.

words.childMeaning: A leader is a person who helps a group decide what to do.
practiceSentences: Nora was the leader of the green team.
A good leader listens to everyone.
The leader showed the class where to line up.
Amal was chosen as leader for the day.
Every group needs a leader to help them start.

words.childMeaning: A team is a group of people who work together.
practiceSentences: Her team was cheering.
The green team had won!
Theo was in the red team.
Every team needs someone to carry the flag.
Amal was the last runner for the green team.

words.childMeaning: A group is a number of people or things together.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin walked between the tables, watching every group work.
A group of birds landed on the wall.
Our group made a poster about insects.
Sit with your group and share the pens.
The group walked to the park together.

words.childMeaning: A community is all the people who live in one place.
practiceSentences: Our community keeps the park clean.
Everyone in the community came to the fair.
Amal is proud of her community.
The community built a new playground.
A community works best when people help.

words.childMeaning: A village is a small group of houses and streets, smaller than a town.
practiceSentences: Every family in the village helped plant trees.
How many people live in this village?
Welcome to our village, Miss Twiga!
The village sits next to a small stream.
Amal lived in a small village beside a river.

words.childMeaning: To shout, or to phone someone to ask for help.
practiceSentences: If there is a fire, you must call for help.
Did you call the doctor about your sore throat?
Amal, call your mum and tell her the good news!
The children call Leila whenever they visit the fire station.
I will call you when the food is ready.

words.childMeaning: To meet means to come together with someone in the same place.
practiceSentences: Shall we meet outside the library at four?
We meet our friends at the gate every morning.
Amal will meet her cousin at the station.
Let us meet under the big tree.
Did you meet the new teacher today?

words.childMeaning: To visit means to go and see a person or a place.
practiceSentences: “Firefighter Leila is coming to visit us today,” she said.
Our class will visit the fire station on Tuesday.
You can visit mine any time, I told him.
“Grandma Hana will visit us tomorrow,” she said.
We visit the library every Saturday.

words.childMeaning: To join means to put things together, or to come into a group.
practiceSentences: The thorax is the middle part, where the legs and wings join on.
Leo wanted to join the football team.
Join the two pieces of paper with glue.
Come and join us at the table.
Nora will join the class after lunch.

words.childMeaning: The way things are arranged, one after another.
practiceSentences: Put the pictures in the right order.
The days of the week have an order.
Amal read the steps in order.
Our names are in order from A to Z.
Leo mixed up the order of the cards.

words.childMeaning: To pass means to go by, or to hand something to someone.
practiceSentences: Please pass the water to Nora.
We pass the market on the way to school.
Leo will pass the ball to Theo.
Amal passed her friend in the corridor.
Pass the pencil to the person beside you.

words.childMeaning: Send means to make something travel or go to a place.
practiceSentences: I will send a letter to my cousin.
Teacher Yasmin will send the list home today.
Amal wants to send a card to Grandma.
Send the ball across the field to Leo.
We send photographs to our family far away.

words.childMeaning: To borrow means to take something and give it back later.
practiceSentences: May I borrow your rubber, please?
Amal went to borrow a book from the library.
Leo asked to borrow a pencil.
You can borrow my coat if you are cold.
We borrow tools from our neighbour.

words.childMeaning: Buy means to get something by paying money for it.
practiceSentences: Did you buy any bread at the shop?
Leo went to buy bread with his mother.
Can we buy some apples, please?
Sami saved his money to buy a book.
After breakfast, Leo walked to the market with his mother to buy bread.

words.childMeaning: Work means the tasks or jobs that people do.
practiceSentences: Leo's father goes to work every morning.
Is this your best work, Maya?
Well done, that is great work!
The class began their partner work quietly.
"Many good people work here," he said.

words.childMeaning: Practise means to do something again and again so you get better at it.
practiceSentences: Did you practise out loud three times?
Amal will practise her speech tonight.
Practise every day, and you will improve!
We practise our spelling every morning.
Leo needs to practise before the race.

words.childMeaning: To agree means to think the same as someone else, or to say yes.
practiceSentences: We agree to share the reading corner every afternoon.
Sami and Theo agree that football is the best game.
Do you agree that we should share the crayons fairly?
"I agree with your plan," said Maya with a smile.
My sister and I rarely agree about which book to read.

words.childMeaning: Helpful means ready to help other people.
practiceSentences: Page two showed a helpful neighbour.
Amal is helpful when the class tidies up.
Thank you for that helpful answer.
A helpful sign showed us the way.
Leo was helpful and carried the heavy box.

words.childMeaning: Happy to talk to people and play with them.
practiceSentences: Nora spoke in a friendly voice to the hurt boy.
Are the pupils friendly at your new school?
“Be friendly to anybody who looks lost,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I try to be friendly to every new pupil in our class.
Nadia the bus driver is friendly, and she waves each morning.

words.childMeaning: Mattering a lot, so that we must care about it.
practiceSentences: Trees are important because they clean the air we breathe.
Why is clean water so important for every family?
“This is important work,” said Adam, lifting the box.
I think it is important to put litter in the bin.
Roots are important, even though we cannot see them.

words.childMeaning: Both means the two of them together.
practiceSentences: Grandma Hana hugged them both.
Both girls finished the race.
Amal and Leo both like reading.
Hold the tray with both hands.
Both windows were open in the warm room.

words.childMeaning: Many means a large number of people or things.
practiceSentences: How many books are on the shelf?
There were many children at the party.
So many stars are out tonight!
Nora has many friends at school.
How many chairs do we need for the visitors?

words.childMeaning: More means a larger number or amount.
practiceSentences: “Tomorrow, let's look for even more.”
“I can read, write and speak more clearly now,” she wrote.
There are more kinds of insects than any other animal.
We need more chairs for the visitors.
Leo wanted more time to finish.

words.childMeaning: Most means nearly all of them, or the largest amount.
practiceSentences: Which page are you most proud of, Amal?
Most of the class chose the blue paper.
This is the most useful book on the shelf.
Most birds build a nest in spring.
Nora ate most of her lunch.

words.childMeaning: Other means the second one, or the ones that are left.
practiceSentences: The other half of the apple is in the bowl.
“Put it on the shelf, next to the other books,” said Amal.
Hold the rope with your other hand.
The other children waited at the gate.
One shoe was here, but where was the other?

words.childMeaning: To keep means to have something and not give it away.
practiceSentences: “Keep watching,” said Adam, turning the ball further.
Fix what needs fixing, and keep the pages that are already strong.
You can keep the pencil I lent you.
Amal will keep her books in this box.
Keep your hands warm inside your gloves.

words.childMeaning: A boot is a strong shoe that covers your foot and ankle.
practiceSentences: Leo pulled on a muddy boot.
One boot was under the bed.
Amal wears a boot on each foot in the rain.
The boot was too small for Theo.
Nora shook the sand out of her boot.

words.childMeaning: Cool means a little bit cold, but not too cold.
practiceSentences: The water in the stream felt cool.
A cool wind blew across the field.
Let the soup cool before you eat it.
Amal sat in the cool shade of the tree.
The evening air was cool and fresh.

words.childMeaning: A person who makes food for other people to eat.
practiceSentences: My mum is a wonderful cook.
Who is the cook at school?
Samira, I will be the cook today!
I help the cook wash the rice.
The cook stirs the big pot.

words.childMeaning: To climb means to go up something using your hands and feet.
practiceSentences: To get up, I climb a wooden ladder.
Leo likes to climb the big tree.
The snail began to climb the wall.
We climb the stairs to our classroom.
Can you climb to the top of the hill?

words.childMeaning: Pull means to move something towards you.
practiceSentences: Pull the rope as hard as you can.
Amal had to pull the heavy door open.
Do not pull the cat's tail.
Leo will pull the cart up the path.
Pull your chair closer to the table.

words.childMeaning: Push means to move something away from you.
practiceSentences: Push the gate gently so it does not bang.
Nora had to push the box across the floor.
Push the button to start the machine.
Do not push in the line, please.
Leo gave the swing a little push.

words.childMeaning: To move means to go from one place to another.
practiceSentences: Today is “Get Up and Move” day at Amal's school.
Please move your bag off the chair.
The shadow will move as the sun goes down.
We watched the snail move slowly along.
Leo had to move to see the board.

words.childMeaning: Drop means to let something fall from your hand.
practiceSentences: Do not drop anything into the tank.
Will you drop the ball if I throw it?
Wow, be careful not to drop that plate!
Adam tried not to drop his schedule.
A drop of rain fell on Amal's nose.

words.childMeaning: To hold means to keep something in your hands.
practiceSentences: Hold this end of the rope while I pull.
Amal will hold the door for Nora.
Can you hold my book for a minute?
Leo likes to hold the baby rabbit.
Hold on tight while the bus moves.

words.childMeaning: To break means to make something come apart in pieces.
practiceSentences: Be careful, or the glass will break.
Do not break the chalk in half.
The old branch began to break.
Leo did not mean to break the cup.
Do not lean on the fence or it will break.

words.childMeaning: To wake means to stop sleeping and open your eyes.
practiceSentences: Amal will wake at six o'clock.
Do not wake the baby, please.
The birds wake me every morning.
Leo tried to wake his brother.
I wake up when the sun comes in.

words.childMeaning: To take means to pick something up and carry it with you.
practiceSentences: In a relay, the runners take turns.
Take one sheet and pass the rest along.
Take your coat, because it is cold.
Amal will take the letter to school.
Please take one card each.

words.childMeaning: To win means to come first or do the best in a game or race.
practiceSentences: Do you think the red team will win?
Leo and Sami want to win together.
We can win, Theo!
We tried our best to win the game.
You do not have to win to have fun.

words.childMeaning: To make an effort to do something, even if it is hard.
practiceSentences: The children got to try on Leila's helmet.
Will you try the new game with me?
Zuri, try to answer this tricky question!
Omar likes to try a new bread recipe every month.
Try it yourself tomorrow.

words.childMeaning: Strong and well, and not feeling ill.
practiceSentences: Nora packs a healthy lunch with rice and beans.
Is a bowl of soup a healthy dinner?
“You look healthy and full of energy today,” said Doctor Sarah.
I feel healthy when I sleep well and drink water.
Clean air and green trees keep our town healthy too.

words.childMeaning: Sick means feeling unwell or having an illness.
practiceSentences: Leo was sick and stayed at home.
Amal felt sick after the long bus ride.
The nurse looks after children who are sick.
A sick plant has yellow leaves.
Tell an adult if you feel sick.

words.childMeaning: Having lots of power in your body or your muscles.
practiceSentences: Adam is strong enough to carry two heavy bags.
Which animal do you think is the strongest?
“Stand tall and make your legs feel strong,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I feel strong after I climb the ladder at the park.
Strong bones grow when we eat well and move often.

words.childMeaning: Weak means not strong.
practiceSentences: The kitten was too weak to stand.

Choose a book from the shelf.
Amal could not choose between the two hats.
You may choose either the red pen or the blue one.

words.childMeaning: To decide means to make up your mind about something.
practiceSentences: Amal could not decide which story to read.
We will decide after lunch.
Leo had to decide quickly.
Let the group decide together.
Decide where to plant the seeds.

words.childMeaning: Also means as well, or in addition.
practiceSentences: She also learned that a turtle carries a hard shell.
Amal can swim and she can also sail.
Leo also wanted to join the team.
The shop sells bread and also milk.
Nora was tired and also very hungry.

words.childMeaning: Yet means up to now, or so far.
practiceSentences: Leo has not finished yet.
Is the bread ready yet?
Amal has not seen the sea yet.
The seeds have not grown yet.
It is not dark yet.

words.childMeaning: Perhaps means maybe, when you are not sure.
practiceSentences: Perhaps it will rain later.
Amal thought perhaps she had left it at home.
Perhaps Leo knows the answer.
We could perhaps go to the park.
Perhaps the bus is late again.

words.childMeaning: Together means with each other, in the same place.
practiceSentences: “Let's read it together,” said Adam.
So the three of them walked together.
They work together and share everything.
“Let's find out together,” said Teacher Yasmin.
The bee makes honey and the ants work together.

words.childMeaning: Apart means away from each other, not together.
practiceSentences: The two friends sat apart in the hall.
Leo took the model apart to fix it.
Keep the wet clothes apart from the dry ones.
The houses stand far apart on the hill.
Amal pulled the pages apart carefully.

words.childMeaning: Whether is used when there is a choice between two things.
practiceSentences: Amal could not tell whether it would rain.
Ask Leo whether he is coming.
I do not know whether the shop is open.
Decide whether to write or to draw.
Nora wondered whether she had won.
